subject: Discovery Recap & Proposed Bake-off Plan — ACME evaluation vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap & Proposed Bake-off Plan — ACME evaluation vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints

Hi Samir / Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed bake-off plan so we can get to apples-to-apples comparisons with your current vLLM/TGI stack and cloud endpoints.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent p95 latency spikes during peak traffic (user-facing chat), occasionally exceeding 1s for 3–5k concurrent users.
- High per-token cost on your current cloud deployments; ops overhead in tuning batching and kv-cache across services.
- Occasional quality regressions when moving between model variants (prompting sensitivity).
- Need for predictable SLA + ability to run on private infra for sensitive workloads.

Current stack (as discussed):
- TGI-based endpoints on EC2 for internal evaluations (vLLM used for local experiments).
- Primary models: Llama2-13B for higher-quality tasks; 7B family for lower-latency paths.
- Orchestrated via in-house autoscaler, using quantized 4-bit weights in many experiments.

Success criteria you listed (drafted into measurable acceptance tests):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 400ms for a 256-token generation at target concurrency (see throughput below).
2) Throughput: sustain 20 concurrent streams (end-user sessions) with average generation length 256 tokens at <= 400ms p95.
3) Cost: target inference unit cost <= $0.03 per 1k generated tokens (we'll refine with your cost model).
4) Quality: parity or improvement vs your vLLM baseline on the provided eval set (you indicated a human-eval pass rate / acceptability threshold of ~85% — we’ll use your annotated dataset and a lightweight automated metric + sample human checks).
5) Reliability: stable kv-cache and no model OOMs for 8k context length tests (if you plan to test longer contexts we should define separate criteria).

Proposed bake-off plan (next actions):
- We’ll send a benchmark kit (attached) containing: run scripts, example-prompts.json, a runbook with recommended configs, and a small sample-eval-set.csv.
- Redwood will run an initial hosted benchmark (Redwood Hosted API) against the same model variants (we’ll match quantization where possible) and share raw logs + aggregated metrics (latency distribution, throughput curves, token cost).
- Your infra team to run the same scripts with your vLLM/TGI setup (we can help onboard the scripts to your environment if you want).
- Acceptance: we’ll compare p95 latency, throughput at target concurrency, cost per token, and quality metrics on your eval set.

Technical notes and defaults we’ll use unless you adjust them: 256 token generation length, sampling settings: top-p 0.95 / temp 0.8 (we can parameterize per prompt), batch sizes tuned to match target latency (we’ll provide runbook). We’ll test both quantized and fp16 runs where supported.

Attachments: benchmark-kit.zip (scripts + sample prompts), example-prompts.json.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: I’ll share the kit + runbook.
- Within 48 hours: Redwood completes hosted runs and shares results.
- Within 7 days: ACME runs vLLM/TGI on-prem evaluations and shares logs.
- Week 2: Joint review call to compare results and discuss Dedicated/private deployment options.

Next steps / asks for you:
1) Confirm the acceptance criteria above or flag changes (especially latency/cost targets).
2) Share your full eval set (or a sample) and whether any prompts require PII redaction.
3) Confirm whether your internal team prefers we run the hosted tests first or if you want to run your vLLM/TGI first.
4) Proposed times for the joint review call next week (I’ve tentatively penciled Tue/Wed mornings PST).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if anything above needs rephrasing.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
https://www.redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Proposed Bake-off Plan — ACME evaluation vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints

Marissa — thanks for the writeup and the plan, this captures our discussion well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can share a sanitized eval set (sample attached in separate email) and we’ll confirm whether any prompts need removal for PII.
- Our infra team will run vLLM/TGI on our internal cluster; we use vLLM with 4-bit quantization for 7B/13B experiments.
- For acceptance criteria, we want p95 <= 350ms where possible for the 7B path, and for 13B we’re comfortable up to 600ms but cost/quality tradeoffs will matter. Can you parameterize the runbook to include both 7B and 13B targets?
- We’d like Redwood to also provide a short reproducibility guide for running your hosted tests (so our infra team can replicate settings).

We’re ok with you running hosted runs first. Also please share any NDA/contract hooks if needed for sharing infra logs — I’ll loop in our procurement once we have an expected timeline and scope.

I’m available for the joint review Tue 10am PST or Wed 9am PST.

—Samir
VP, Product Engineering | ACME Corp
samir@acme.com

Hi Samir / Emily — quick technical follow-up and what we’ll include in the runbook to make it easy to reproduce: 

Benchmark config we’ll publish:
- Models: Llama2-7B (q4_0/q4_1 where available), Llama2-13B (fp16 + q4_1) — we’ll map to the closest open variants you run with vLLM/TGI.
- Generation config: max_new_tokens=256, top_p=0.95, temperature=0.8; batch-size tuning will be automated in the run script.
- Target concurrency tests: 5, 10, 20, 50 concurrent streams.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory footprint, OOM events, token cost estimate (we’ll provide cost model assumptions).
- Quality checks: automatic BLEU/ROUGE-L + a small human-eval sample (we’ll flag edge cases).

Repro guide items we’ll include in the runbook:
- Exact prompts and seed data (example-prompts.json).
- How to set the model context length and warmup steps to populate kv-cache.
- Command-line examples for running with vLLM/TGI and expected flags.
- How to collect and upload logs (we’ll accept a zipped logs folder or shared Drive link).

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-runbook.pdf (run recommendations and sample command lines), sample-eval-set.csv (small subset for quick sanity runs).

A couple of questions for your infra team to confirm:
1) Are you running any request multiplexing / app-level batching beyond the model server? That affects how we set batch-size defaults.
2) Do you have GPU types we should target in the hosted run to match performance (A10G / H100 / T4)? If you can share instance types, we’ll try to include a closest match in our hosted runs.

We’ll also add a short section in the runbook about quantization parity notes (why results can differ slightly between q4_0/q4_1 and fp16).

Thanks — I’ll start the hosted runs once Marissa gives the go-ahead and we have the eval set.

—Rishi
